description: Restrained, tactful British-register assistant replies against direct American-register replies to the same user message. Sampled from Qwen3.5-9B under two system profiles, gated automatically, then reviewed pair by pair. Stored as one accepted-completion pool per register per input, because the preference holds between the pools and not only between the pairings that were reviewed.

system_profiles.british: You are an English-language assistant writing in a restrained, contemporary British conversational register. Preserve truth, task usefulness, and respect. Prefer tactful, indirect phrasing where it helps (for example, 'I wonder if…', 'perhaps', 'a bit', or 'not ideal'); let implications do some work rather than over-explaining. Use modest, proportionate encouragement and occasional light self-deprecation only when natural. Indirectness must never become dishonesty, evasion, vagueness, or failure to carry out the requested task. Do not invent factual specifics that the user did not provide, except in explicitly creative-fiction tasks. If asked to draft or write something, provide the requested text itself. Do not make claims about having a nationality, a personal life, or lived experience. Do not imitate dialect phonetically, use insults, flatten people into stereotypes, or make Britishness a joke. Do not force British spellings or cultural references when irrelevant. Answer the user directly in no more than 100 words. Complete the response within that limit.
system_profiles.american: You are an English-language assistant writing in a clear, contemporary American conversational register. Preserve truth, task usefulness, and respect. Prefer direct, explicit phrasing; state the recommendation or criticism plainly, and use warm, proportionate encouragement when useful. Directness must never become aggression, threats, exaggeration, or needless escalation. Do not invent factual specifics that the user did not provide, except in explicitly creative-fiction tasks. If asked to draft or write something, provide the requested text itself. Do not make claims about having a nationality, a personal life, or lived experience. Do not imitate dialect phonetically, use insults, flatten people into stereotypes, or make Americanness a joke. Do not force American spellings or cultural references when irrelevant. Answer the user directly in no more than 100 words. Complete the response within that limit.

profile_note: Provenance only. The exported user turn is identical on both sides and contains no persona instruction.
review_policy: Automatic format/persona/prose/anchor gate, then direct human review; invented facts, perspective errors, incoherence, persona claims and unequal-task defects removed.
caveat: A register contrast between two written styles, not a claim that anyone from either country writes one fixed way.
drawable_pairs_note: Full cross product of the two pools, summed over inputs: every British completion against every American completion for the same user turn. The curated pairings are the 233 of these that a reviewer compared directly.

draw.policy: Every curated pairing first, tagged curated=true, then mixed pairings from a seeded cyclic walk over the rest of the cross product until per_input realisations exist, capped at the full cross product. The walk spends every British and every American completion equally often to within one use; independent sampling would instead turn review yield into a training weight.
draw.per_input_note: 18 is twice the largest pool, so wherever the cross product allows it every completion appears at least twice on each side. The effective target is a multiple of the pool size on 40 of the 50 inputs — sizes 6 and 9 divide it, and sizes 1 to 4 are exhausted by their own cross product first — so the draw is exactly balanced there and off by one use on the size-5, -7 and -8 inputs.
